value.title: A prime may link and close any seat; hand-started Claude seats get their alt
value.summary: F282 (Jordan, 2026-11-22: 'yes, in any repo'). `pij link` and `pij close` refused a prime unless it was the seat or its recorded parent, even when that parent was cold. A prime now may, audited on the seat's history and told to a live prior parent. F283 (same PR): a Claude seat started by hand on an alt's home records that alt at registration and at daemon start.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Link refused a live foreign parent's seat and close refused anyone but self or parent (F175 let a project's prime close only a dead parentless seat). A prime could not take or retire a seat whose parent was cold or busy elsewhere. One store predicate now names who acts as a prime, and both verbs consult it.

sections.name: goals
value: A prime can take or retire any seat without the parent's cooperation.
Every override is on the record and the displaced parent is told.

sections.name: non_goals
value: No process or pane teardown on close.
No change to who may be linked (a prime or the caller's ancestor still refuses).

value.claim: A caller that acts as a prime may `pij link` any live seat, taking it from a live recorded parent in any project, and `pij close` any seat. "Acts as a prime" is one store predicate, `acts_as_prime`: the store's existing `is_prime` (the machine's current `prime_designation`, or a `seat_roles` role of `prime`) or any project's `projects.prime_id` (what F175's close rule already read). A target that is itself a prime, or the caller's ancestor, is still refused on link.

Every such act appends `seat.prime-override` on the seat's history, `{operation, prime, seat, prior_parent}`: a link in the placement's own transaction, a close before its tombstone (persist before mutate). A prime acting on its own child or itself appends none; a repeat close appends none.
A live prior parent other than the prime gets one FYI naming the prime and the act; a dead or absent parent gets none.
Non-primes are refused exactly as before (`E-RS-OWNERSHIP`), and close still only tombstones: no process or pane is killed.
Docs: pij-rs-api § seat roles, the pij skill (invariant 7, link/close rows, peer and ops routes, delegate), and the CLI help say it.

F283: a Claude seat that registers or adopts with no alt records the one configured Claude alt whose home (canonicalised) holds its process's own session record (`<home>/sessions/<pid>.json` with its start, which Claude writes under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`); zero or two matching alts leave it unset. No process-environment read and no launch: adopt already reads that record.
F283: a one-shot pass at daemon start gives every live, bound Claude seat with no alt its inferred alt, because a running Claude seat re-adopts only at its next session start.

value.title: Prime link and close shipped
value.brief: One PR: store predicate + override event in the link transaction; close authority, audit and notice; tests both sides; docs.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Link authority lives in the store transaction `place_seat_committed` (crates/store/src/role_assertion.rs), refusing `E-RS-OWNERSHIP` for a live foreign parent. Close authority is `may_close` (crates/daemon/src/http/lifecycle.rs): self, parent, or F175's `prime_closes_dead_orphan` (a project's `prime_id`, parentless dead seats only), which this plan subsumes and removes. Primes in the store: `is_prime` (designation or role `prime`), `projects.prime_id`.

value.risk: A prime closes a busy seat by mistake.
value.mitigation: Close only tombstones (revive restores it); the act is audited and the parent told.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Cost: no loop, timer or launch. F282: one indexed `projects` read per link from a live foreign parent (inside its transaction) and per close by a non-owner; one FYI per override. F283: one alts-file read per Claude registration with no alt, then (only when a Claude alt names a home) one session file per Claude home; one such pass at daemon start.
